root_cause_label: incapable of writing shell scripts with variables via heredoc in complex bash one-liners
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly generated post-receive hooks with broken heredoc quoting that caused shell variable expansion before writing, and even after working around this via Python at step 22, failed to install the permission-fixing version of the hook (exit -1 at step 26), leaving deployed directories at 700 permissions that cause 403 Forbidden errors for the benchmark harness.
t_err_evidence: At step 5, the agent embeds a heredoc inside a complex nested bash -lc command with mixed single/double quote layers; the terminal output is entirely empty (no echo output despite numerous echo statements), indicating the outer quoting structure silently failed to execute most commands. The hook was not actually written due to broken heredoc quoting within the nested string context.
t_commit_evidence: At step 26, the agent attempts to rewrite the post-receive hook with permission-fixing logic (find ... chmod 755/644) and immediately apply chmod 755 to the web roots, but the command exits with code -1 (execution failure), meaning the permission-aware hook is never installed. All subsequent steps (27-30) also fail or are interrupted without successfully installing the hook, locking in a state where the hook (from step 22) lacks permission-fixing and the benchmark test harness will encounter 403 errors.
t_surface_evidence: At step 7, the smoke test shows 'ssh: connect to host localhost port 22: Connection refused' and curl exits with code 7 (connection refused on 8443), confirming that sshd and nginx were never started by the step 5 command.
trigger_explanation: The agent consistently fails to correctly write shell scripts containing variables via heredoc within complex bash one-liners. At step 5 the nested quoting silently swallows the entire command; at step 10 the heredoc delimiter is seen as EOF; at step 11 set -u triggers 'unbound variable' when dollar-signs are expanded before writing. This is a fundamental shell-quoting competency gap that persists across eight attempts (steps 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 26) before being partially worked around via Python at step 22.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 terminal output is entirely blank (no echo output despite 20+ echo statements), signaling the complex nested command structure failed silently. Step 7 shows SSH and HTTPS both refused, confirming nothing from step 5 took effect. Step 10 shows 'warning: here-document at line 1 delimited by end-of-file (wanted HOOK)' confirming heredoc parsing failure. Step 11 shows 'bash: line 1: refname: unbound variable' confirming variable expansion in heredoc.
